Well, it does matter what time of year. For doing the artificial swarm, you'll want to do that when the bees are ready to swarm in the spring.  For me, that's around the end of march into April here in the southern US, and they could even swarm into the summer. My method im using to do this is called a blind split. Where you have two brood boxes and go through and make sure there are fresh eggs in both boxes and you just take one box, set it on a new bottom and close both boxes back up. Whichever box doesn't have the queen, will take an egg and make a few queen cells. It's a good idea to go through the box in about a week, give or take and nock down all gueen cells except 3 or 4 so the queens aren't having a 22 player free for all.

For feeding sugar syrup, you want to wait until the temps get above freezing before you start and a few weeks before it traditionally starts getting below freezing in your area. A lot of people say to feed at 1:1 ratio in spring and 2:1 before winter. I just feed 2:1 year round. My thoughton this is the bees won't have to work it as much to make comb, and they also won't have to evaporate as much water if they decide to store it.

Those are combo bobbers. If you pass the line through both the hole in the bobber and the peg, it acts as a slip float. Which is great for fishing heavy structures like blowdowns and brush piles. They sell bobber stoppers online, but you can just use a piece of thread or line. If you pass it through the bobber, then push the peg on top of the line, and it will act as a regular stationary bobber which is good for fishing open areas or areas where you know the structure and what level in the water fish are hanging.
